architecture.techLabel: AI Technical Architecture — 五层系统架构
architecture.techIntro: The product is the Insight Engine (Layer 3). The chatbot is the UI. RAG knowledge base is table stakes — not the moat.

layers.name: Evidence Graph · RAG Knowledge Base
layers.desc: Structured scientific claims from Brenner (NAD+, metabolism), Gunter (women's health, pending), dermatology literature · evidence_level tiers: rct / clinical_guideline / expert_opinion / emerging · PostgreSQL + pgvector · Not the moat — table stakes

layers.name: User Longitudinal Data · On-Device
layers.desc: Labs, wearables, skin photos, symptoms, interventions, outcomes — stored locally encrypted (Core Data / Room + SQLCipher) · Tiered consent: Tier 0 default on-device, Tier 1 opt-in encrypted upload, Tier 2 opt-in research contribution

layers.name: DrRuby Insight Engine · N-of-1 Analytics
layers.desc: Change detection (moving average, z-score) · Intervention Graph (what worked for this user, with lag and confidence) · Proprietary scores: Skin Age Score, Metabolic Score, Recovery Score, Inflammation Score, Hormonal Stability Index · V1: rule-based + statistical · V2: Bayesian attribution · Patent candidates: scoring methodology + Intervention Graph structure

layers.name: Recommendation Engine
layers.desc: Combines Layer 3 insights + Layer 1 evidence → structured recommendation object · This runs before the LLM, not inside it · Output is structured data, not prose

layers.name: Conversation Interface · UI Only
layers.desc: LLM API (Claude / GPT-4o) translates Layer 3+4 structured output into natural language + citations · Proactive push when Insight Engine detects change · Conversational data logging ("I started NR today" → writes to Intervention Graph) · Hybrid UI: score cards + chat · FDA guardrails embedded in system prompt

architecture.moatNote: Why this can't be replicated in 3 weeks: Layer 1 (RAG on PubMed) can. Layers 3–4 cannot — because they require months of a user's longitudinal data and the Intervention Graph that grows with it. The data is the moat. Brenner's role is Scientific Advisory Board — he defines scoring methodology, not claim validation.
